name: Chattahoochee Bend State Park
note: RVs go in Campground 1 (sites 101-126); Campground 2's electric sites are short tent/pop-up pads. The riverfront platform and walk-in sites are tent-only. Boat ramp on the Chattahoochee; the river is ~200 m north of Campground 1 through woods. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $32 a night for an electric/water back-in site, $36 for a pull-through or a host-designated site; the same on a weekday and a Saturday (November 2026, June 2027). Walk-in tent and platform sites $20, backcountry $11. Vehicles need the $10 ParkPass. Read 2026-10-29.
field_notes.Sites: 37 electric RV/tent sites in two campgrounds. Campground 1 (sites 101-126, 26 sites) takes rigs to 40 ft, 8 of them pull-through; Campground 2's 11 electric sites (201-206, 219-223) are capped at 15 ft. Sites 101, 126 and 201 are marked Host, so 24 public sites take a 23-ft rig. 12 walk-in tent, 8 river platform and 8 backcountry sites besides.

name: Georgia Veterans Memorial State Park
note: GA state park on Lake Blackshear near Cordele; the campground is run by Lake Blackshear Resort (Coral Hospitality), the park's concession; check in with the resort. Boat ramp and fishing pier next to the campground. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Lake Blackshear Resort (Coral Hospitality), the park's concession, takes campsite reservations at 229-276-1004; sites are reserved by number. Its online engine was switched off when read 2026-10-29 ('not taking reservations through this website at this time. Please contact the site directly'). Not on the state parks' ReserveAmerica site.
field_notes.Fees: $55 a night for a 30-amp site away from the water, $60 for 50-amp or full hookups, $65-70 on the waterfront, the same on a Saturday (January 2027). The campground books through Lake Blackshear Resort, the park's concession. Vehicles need the $10 ParkPass. Read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 82 sites for tents, trailers or RVs; lakeside sites along the shore where a boat can be pulled up to the site. Every site takes an RV up to 50 ft. Plus two pioneer group campsites and glamping safari tents.

name: Jacks River Fields Campground
note: USFS Chattahoochee NF, Conasauga RD, on the South Fork of the Jacks River. Access is 15+ mi of steep, narrow, winding gravel road whose condition changes with the weather; FS 64 is closed west of the campground January-March, so it is reached only from Blue Ridge then. Also accommodates horses/mules (corrals and horse-trailer parking at the back). Nearest gas and store 16 mi away in Blue Ridge; cell service very limited. --Claude

field_notes.Season: January through March the campground is reachable only from Blue Ridge (FS 64 closed west of the campground).
field_notes.Booking: First come, first served only: claim a site in person, then pay at the fee tube (cash/check) or with the Recreation.gov app's scan-and-pay (works offline).
field_notes.Sites: Forest Service: 'Road and campground access limited to recreational vehicles less than 24 feet'; Recreation.gov: 'Travel Trailers over 25 feet are not recommended'. The catalog lists no per-site lengths or equipment.

name: Victoria Campground
note: USACE Mobile District campground on Allatoona Lake near Woodstock, with a boat ramp, dock and swim beach; the premium sites (13, 14, 17, 19, 21-26, 47-56) are the waterfront ones. --Claude

Booking: min stay 2 nights on weekends, 3 on holidays

field_notes.Season: Seasonal, roughly mid-March to mid-October. 2026: last night October 17, no dates offered November-February; 2027 dates read 'Not Available' through March 10 and are not yet released after that.
field_notes.Booking: Two-night weekend and three-night holiday-weekend minimums; 14 nights in any 30 across the Corps' Allatoona campgrounds. Everyone checks in at the gatehouse; gate closed 10:30 pm - 7 am; three vehicles per site; check-in 4 pm (7 am if the site is empty), check-out 3 pm.
field_notes.Fees: $30 a night at a standard electric/water site, $34 at the premium waterfront sites (13, 14, 17, 19, 21-26, 47-56); the same in 2026 and 2027. The one tent-only site (11) is $24.
field_notes.Sites: 75 numbered sites, all but tent-only site 11 with 50 A electric and water; 71 are bookable on recreation.gov (driveways 30-80 ft, so all take a 23-ft rig; 27 pull-throughs). The Corps lists 2 sites with sewer too, but no bookable site carries sewer.

name: Camp South RV Park
note: Family-owned farm RV park in a pine woods, 18903 Kermit Rd, Metter, about 1 mi off I-16 Exit 98; the last stretch of Kermit Rd is dirt. Playground, dog park, trails, fishing pond and farm animals. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $40 a night in June-October 2026 (RV Life reviews); the park has no working website (2026-10-29). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED: $40 a night in RV Life reviews of stays in June, July and October 2026 ($34 in October 2023); the operator posts no rate (its website is a parked domain).

name: Catfish Creek RV Campground
note: Owner-run pull-through sites under pecan trees on US-301 between Claxton and Glennville; some road noise. Call ahead if arriving after 6 pm. Restrooms were closed in late 2025. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $30 a night in 2025-2026 (RV Life reviews); the park has no website (2026-10-29). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED: $30 a night in RV Life reviews of stays in November 2025, July 2026 and August 2026 ($20 cash in 2022-2023); the operator has no web page.

name: Georgia International Horse Park RV Park
note: City of Conyers' Georgia International Horse Park (1996 Olympic equestrian venue). RV lots by the stable and Walker Arena complexes. General RV park, not horse-only: non-event guests take nightly stays by phone, subject to the show calendar. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Event and show guests book through the event promoter. Anyone else calls the Horse Park office (770-860-4190, Mon-Fri 8-5) in advance; availability depends on the show schedule.
field_notes.Fees: $32 a night per RV, 30- or 50-amp, on the park's 2026 registration form; showers included. No weekend or seasonal difference published.
field_notes.Sites: '140+ sites' in the Main RV Lot (near the Stable Complex and Walker Arena) and the Barn 6 RV lot; the lot map mixes water+electric sites with full-hookup ones. No site lengths published.

name: Wildwood Park
note: Columbia County (GA) park on Clarks Hill/J. Strom Thurmond Lake at Appling. Three camping areas on the lake plus primitive sites; boat ramps, beach, disc golf. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booked online on Columbia County's Rec1 catalog (Wildwood Park tab, Areas 1-3) or through the park office.
field_notes.Fees: Columbia County: regular campsite $25/night (the booking catalog charges every site $25, any residency); seniors 55+ $22; primitive $15 per tent, group primitive $50 (non-profit groups, arranged with the park supervisor). The park's entry fee ($3 per car or truck a day, $6 with a boat; $30 annual pass) is listed separately and the county doesn't say whether campers pay it. Dump station $5. Cancelling 3+ days out costs one night; inside 3 days no refund.
field_notes.Sites: Three camping areas: Area 1 36 sites (01-35 plus 05a), Area 2 15 (36-51), Area 3 10 (52-61). The county's site descriptions give lengths of 40-80 ft (two sites unstated), so every site takes a 23-ft rig; the Area 1 map marks some pull-throughs. 27 primitive sites are booked separately.

name: Traders Hill County Park
note: Charlton County recreation area on the St. Marys River near Folkston (1388 Tracys Ferry Rd), by the Okefenokee NWR; sites in open woods a short walk from the river, boat ramp and fishing pier. Some sites share a sewer connection. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $30 water/electric, $35 full hookup (Campendium review, February 2024; $30 paid November 2025); the county has no web page for the park (2026-10-29). Camper review October 2026: bathhouse 'very filthy and in severe disrepair'. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: No reservations reported; no county booking channel or page found. Call the county before going.
field_notes.Fees: CAMPER-REPORTED, no county page posts a rate: $30 a night for water and electric, $35 for full hookups (Campendium review, February 2024: 'The rates are $35 full hookup, $30 water and electric. Tent with power $20, tent primitive $10'); a November 2025 stay paid $30. Tent sites not counted.

name: Manatee Springs State Park
note: Three campground loops (Magnolia 1, Magnolia 2, Hickory) within walking distance of the spring; sewer only in Magnolia 1, and Hickory's sites are sold as tent-only. Glamping sites in Hickory Loop are booked through the park's concessionaire. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $27 a night for an RV: the $20 campsite fee plus Florida's $7 nightly utility fee for RVs (tent campers pay $20), plus tax and a $6.70 reservation fee per reservation. No out-of-state rate; Florida residents 65 and over get half off the campsite fee. The park's Hours & Fees page and Florida's fee page, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 80 campsites in three loops. 'Maximum RV length = 40 feet on Sites, 5, 7 and 37'; Reserve Florida lists Magnolia 1 sites at 15-40 ft (4 pull-through) and Magnolia 2 at 20-35 ft; Hickory's 10 sites and 14 Magnolia 1 sites are tent-only.

name: O'Leno State Park
note: Two loops, Magnolia and Dogwood, with a playground in Magnolia; the park warns the loops are compact with extremely narrow roads, so larger RVs may need extensive maneuvering into the back-in sites. Coords pinned to Magnolia loop (river-closest). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $25 a night for an RV: the $18 campsite fee plus Florida's $7 nightly utility fee for RVs (tent campers pay $18), plus tax and a $6.70 reservation fee per reservation. No out-of-state rate; Florida residents 65 and over get half off the campsite fee. The park's Hours & Fees page and Florida's fee page, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 61 campsites in the Magnolia and Dogwood loops; site sizes vary to a 50-ft maximum (Reserve Florida: Dogwood 15-42 ft, Magnolia 20-50 ft, one pull-through in Magnolia). The park warns the loops are compact with extremely narrow roads and that larger RVs may need extensive maneuvering into the back-in sites.

name: Dinner Island Ranch WMA - Hammock Camp
note: FWC Wildlife Management Area. Hammock Camp: primitive sites under an oak hammock, 10 for tents/campers/small RVs (1 ADA) and 7 tent-only; no amenities beyond a vault toilet. Gravel access road off CR 833 (short, washboardy, can get muddy after heavy rain). Best dry season Nov-Apr.

field_notes.Booking: Every camper needs a free FWC permit/site reservation, made online (WebReserv) or by calling the South Regional Office at 561-625-5122 (Mon-Fri 8-5), up to 14 days ahead; no camping outside the designated camps. 14 consecutive days in a month, then 14 days must pass; a site left empty 48 hours may be cancelled.
field_notes.Sites: Hammock Camp: 17 primitive sites, 7 tent-only and 10 for tents, campers or small RVs (one an ADA RV site). One RV and one tent per RV site, two vehicles per site; no generators at sites 1-6. FWC gives no length limit.

name: Long Pine Key Campground
note: Everglades NP drive-in campground ~7 mi inside the main (Homestead) entrance off the park road. Run by the Flamingo Adventures / Everglades Guest Services concession (NOT recreation.gov).

field_notes.Booking: Booked through the park concessioner (Flamingo Adventures / Everglades Guest Services), online or at 855-708-2207, not recreation.gov. NPS: 'Reservations are available for RV's and tents along with first come first serve sites.' Register by 10 a.m., check-out 12 p.m.
field_notes.Fees: $33 Mon-Thu, $38.50 Fri-Sun.

name: Clay County Fairgrounds RV Park
note: County-operated RV park at the Clay County Fairgrounds (2463 SR-16 W, Green Cove Springs); gated/coded entry, big-rig friendly. Open year-round for transient stays (30-day max), closed during the spring fair (so NOT event-only camping). RV-only park with no kid amenities. RV Life 8.3*/35 reviews; Good Sam listed. Operated through the county fairgrounds office (Fairgrounds@claycountygov.com), hence ownership=local. --Claude  Hipcamp listing switched off (not bookable) as of 2026-10-10; book through the fairgrounds office by phone/email. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Clay County FY 26/27 schedule of fees: fairgrounds RV hookups $40 a night each, plus sales tax and the Tourist Development Tax. Booked through the fairgrounds office by phone or email.

name: Kymulga Grist Mill Park
note: City of Childersburg park (Childersburg Historic Preservation Commission) on Talladega Creek by the historic grist mill and covered bridge; 12 water/electric sites (30-amp), RVs to 32 ft, restrooms/showers. Reservable. --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $40 a night for a full-hookup site in March 2024 (RV Life review); the park has no operator web page and kymulgagristmill.com is for sale (2026-10-11). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: An RV Life reviewer paid $40 a night in March 2024 for a full-hookup site by the creek. No operator rate page (kymulgagristmill.com is for sale); confirm by phone.

name: Point Mallard Park
note: City of Decatur Parks & Recreation campground near the Tennessee River; 217 shaded full-hookup sites (water/sewer/electric) plus 6 tent sites, laundry, store, dump station. Golf, water park, trails at the park. Reservable. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights (Reservations (section A, 52 sites) require a two-night minimum.; pointmallardpark.com, 2026-10-10). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Reservations (section A, 52 sites) require a two-night minimum. Kept with the minimum marked, per AWH 2026-10-10.

name: Camping World Campground of Oxford
note: Year-round transient campground at the Camping World dealership off I-20 (exit 188), Oxford; long pull-through sites, full hookups. Booked via Good Sam / Camping World network (no standalone site). --Claude  CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $40-44 a night in April-October 2026 (RV Life reviews); the campground has no web page of its own (2026-10-11). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: RV Life reviewers paid $43 (April 2026), $40 (May 2026), $40 and $44 (August 2026) and $43 (October 2026). The campground has no page of its own; confirm by phone.

name: Lakeshore Cabins & RV
note: Family-owned park on a Lewis Smith Lake peninsula near Jasper; ~13 full-hookup RV pads (20/30/50A) plus 8 cabins, nightly, all ages. Cabins are the waterfront units; RV pads sit back on the peninsula with lake views. --Claude  MINIMUM STAY: 2 nights (Two-night minimum (three nights for holidays) on cabins and RV sites.; lakeshorecabinsandrv.com, 2026-10-10). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Two-night minimum (three nights for holidays) on cabins and RV sites. Kept with the minimum marked, per AWH 2026-10-10.
field_notes.Fees: RV upper sites (partial lake view) $32 + tax, lower lake-view sites $38 + tax; up to 4 people, $3.50 each extra; two-night minimum (three on holidays).

name: Calling Panther Lake
note: MDWFP State Fishing Lake 5 mi W of Crystal Springs off New Zion Rd. 23 camping pads with electric/water/sewer plus primitive camping; shower houses/bathrooms. Trophy-bass lake.

field_notes.Fees: $25 a night (21 sites (and 2 accessible ones) with electric, water and sewer). Campers 62 and older and disabled campers $15. First come, first served: no reservations; the daily camping permit includes fishing and boat launching for up to 8 people. MDWFP's state fishing lake fees (rate sheet effective 2023-06-23), read 2026-10-12.

name: Lake Lamar Bruce
note: MDWFP State Fishing Lake ~1.5 mi NE of Saltillo off US-45 (Lee Co.); 300-acre lake — the only public water in MS stocked with rainbow trout. 11 sites with water + electric plus primitive camping; concrete boat ramp with courtesy piers, 5 handicap-access fishing piers, pavilion, restrooms/showers. Call the state lake office.

field_notes.Fees: $22 a night for one of the 11 sites with electric and water; primitive camping without electricity $17. Campers 62 and older and disabled campers $15. First come, first served: no reservations; the daily camping permit includes fishing and boat launching for up to 8 people. MDWFP's state fishing lake fees (rate sheet effective 2023-06-23), read 2026-10-12.

name: Lake Monroe
note: MDWFP State Fishing Lake between Aberdeen and Amory off Hwy 45 (Monroe County) on 99-acre Lake Monroe. 14 camping pads with electric/water (30-amp), kayak launch, boat ramp, two handicapped fishing piers, restrooms with showers. Call the State Lake office.  Closed until further notice: MDWFP's lake page says camping is not available (read 2026-10-12). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $22 a night (12 sites with electric and water). Campers 62 and older and disabled campers $15. First come, first served: no reservations; the daily camping permit includes fishing and boat launching for up to 8 people. The lake's page says camping is currently not available and the campground is closed until further notice. MDWFP's state fishing lake fees (rate sheet effective 2023-06-23), read 2026-10-12.

name: Grassy Road Cabins and Camping
note: Privately owned 23-acre property near the Buffalo National River at Marshall (8597 AR-27). 10 full-hookup RV sites with 20/30/50 amp water/sewer, level gravel pads; plus 8 tent sites, 2 cabins, bathhouse, stocked fishing pond. RV sites booked online through the park's Firefly reservations page. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Full-hookup RV sites (20/30/50 amp) start at $45 a night; electric tent sites from $30 and primitive tent sites from $22. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Outdoor Living Center RV Park
note: Privately owned RV park at 10 Outdoor Place, Russellville, just off I-40. ~50 full-hookup sites (30/50 amp), 24 pull-thrus, max ~60 ft, restrooms, rec hall, pool, playground, WiFi/cable. No official site found (Good Sam listing in lieu). Camper-reported rate: $40-43 a night (Campendium, August 2025 and April 2026). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Campendium reviewers paid $43 a night in August 2025 and $40 in April 2026.

name: Black Beach Municipal Campground
note: City of Silver Bay campground on Lake Superior's North Shore, beside Black Beach Park, with an ATV trail from the campground.  It opened in 2020, so the trees are still young and shade is thin.  34 sites have full hookups and 15 electric only; the electric-only sites take rigs up to 35 feet.  The nearest boat launch is at the Silver Bay Marina, about 5 miles south. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: From the city's rates page (read 2026-10-13): sites with electric only (20/30 amp, rigs up to 35 feet) $34 Sunday to Thursday and $39 on Friday and Saturday, or $36 and $41 from June through September; full-hookup sites (20/30/50 amp) $47 and $50, or $49 and $52 from June through September.  By the week, $209 with electric only and $285 with full hookups.  Campspot's booking engine, closed for the season from October 11, 2026, quoted the same $34 and $47 for October 20, plus a $2 'Reservation Fee' once per stay.  The city's page also lists a $10 non-refundable reservation fee, a $10 fee to change a reservation and an optional $10 to lock in a chosen site.

name: City of Fergus Falls DeLagoon Campground
note: City of Fergus Falls park campground on Pebble Lake, rebuilt in 2025 to 42 RV sites (10 full-hookup, 32 water+electric) plus 8 tent sites, new bathhouse and dump, boat landing. Reservations online only (Campspot), 7-night maximum. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Water and electric RV sites $50 a night, full hook-up $60, tent sites with water and electric $25; in October and April every site is $25. Reservations online only, 7-night maximum. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.
